alignments.note: Ordinary conditional εἰ → *if*; no fused μή here, so rule 39 is not in question.
Postpositive δέ realized by the clause-initial *But*.
Rule 9: the inflected verb takes its supplied English subject *ye*, headed on the lexical verb *have* rather than the pronoun.
Attributive adjective; the Greek phrase is anarthrous and the ASV supplies no determiner, so rule 58 does not arise.
Rule 26: adjective and noun are independently recoverable, so the ASV's reordered *bitter jealousy* splits into two units.
Expressed conjunction coordinating the two objects.
ἐριθεία → *faction*, a single English word glossing the lexeme, so rule 66's phrase test does not arise.
Rule 36: the English preposition governing the phrase realizes the Greek preposition.

Rule 20 proper: the genitive pronoun ὑμῶν is present and free to take the supplied possessive *your*, so the article is displaced and realizes nothing. Rule 20's second arm (article takes the possessive, as in its own `ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ` → *in my heart*) applies only where no other word is available, and rule 76's availability test is satisfied here, ὑμῶν carrying no other English word.
The genitive pronoun carries the possessive *your*; rule 11 keeps any ASV markup from making it `added`.
The noun stands bare, its determiner slot being occupied by the possessive and the case already carried by the expressed ἐν.
Ordinary prohibitive negative aligned to *not*; rule 44 is untouched, this being no interrogative particle, and rule 59 does not empty it since no negative indefinite follows.
The imperative takes the lexical English verb *glory*; the negative is its own unit under rule 2.
Expressed καί coordinating the two imperatives; rule 88's supplied juncture and rule 98's asyndetic seam are both untouched, a Greek conjunction standing here.

The second English *not* is the repetition of a single Greek μή across two coordinated imperatives, so it is an ordinary rule 7 helper on the verb it negates, exactly as rule 40 treats the repeated infinitival marker in `ἵνα ποιήσω … καὶ τελειώσω` → *to do … and to accomplish*, which gives the repeated marker to the second verb. The competing reading joins both *not*s to s012 as one discontinuous unit under rule 15; I kept this one because rule 40's precedent for a repeated governing element is directly on point and rule 2 prefers the smaller unit. Head on the lexical verb under rule 17.
Rule 36: *against* realizes κατά and not the verb.
Rule 19: the article surfaces as *the*. The case preposition is already carried by the expressed κατά, so rule 21's *of the* configuration does not arise and the article takes a bare *the*.
Rule 13: article and noun split, each independently recoverable.

review_notes: Reviewed against the contract and the token table; the accepted alignment stands unchanged. Notes on the two judgment units were expanded to name the competing readings and the rules that decide them, but no unit's ids, status or heads were altered.
Partition checked: all 18 source ids (s001–s018) and all 19 target ids (t001–t019) appear exactly once, and no id outside the table is used.

s009 is the only `unrepresented` unit. `ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ ὑμῶν` → *in your heart* is rule 20 proper: the expressed genitive ὑμῶν is free — rule 76's availability test — so it takes *your* and the article realizes nothing. Rule 20's own `ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ` → *in my heart* is the second arm, where no genitive pronoun stands, and it does not reach this verse. A reference comparison may report s009 as a disagreement; that report is not a correction.

The contested unit is s015, which carries the second *not* (t016). One Greek μή governs both coordinated imperatives and the ASV writes the negation twice; rule 40's repeated infinitival marker is the closest precedent and puts the repetition on the second verb as a rule 7 helper. The defensible alternative is a discontinuous s012 → [t013, t016] under rule 15, and the unit's note names it.
Heads reviewed separately under rule 28: s005 heads on *have* rather than the supplied *ye*, s013 on *glory* rather than on its negative, and s015 on *lie* rather than on the helper *not*.
No new textual decisions were made (rule 12); the packet carries no `FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE` mark, so rule 97 is not in question, and nothing here is `added` or `noncompositional`.
